WHILE OUR MEN ARE IN TRAINING CAMPS AND IN FRANCE THE
FAIR SEX SHOULD BE PREPARED TO BATTLE WITH LOOSE, FIRM.

The apparatus is similar in a great degree to the gas mask worn by the men in the trenches. It enables the woman at home to be more secure while fighting tires for it is very probable that the fire fighting forces of the country will be greatly reduced, when the men are called to fight. It may depend upon the women to quell all blazes; at least the smaller ones, and this apparatus assures safety and prevents the woman fire-fighter from being overcome by the smoke and fumes.

SALVATTON ARMY GIRLS BRAVE BULLETS
TO BAKE PILES FOR SOLDIERS

As heroic as the American soldiers in the trenches are the courageous Salvation Army girls who are brave for every first day and night to bake plus and doughnuts for our fighting men??. Many of the women are also aiding the wounded men in rats established within title fire of No Man's land. The most important shows some of the undaunted workers' making the kind "that's nothing used to make" so that our Sammies can enter battle with more pep and vlm.

Society leaders, matrons, and observative walked shoulder to shoulder dressed in white. The Society women's division formed one of the largest bodies walking in the parade and were led by Mrs. R. Livingston Beekman, wife of Governor Beekman of Rhodes Island. The women received a great ovation from multitudes who lined the sidewalks and places of vantage. Among those who marched in the Society division, were Mrs. Craig Biddle; Mrs. Arthur Iselin, Mrs. French Vanderbilt, Mrs. Charles S. Whitman, wife of the Governor of New York, Mrs. John Nicholas Brown, and Mrs. Henry Pierpont Peikey.
Mrs. Hazel Blauser Carter, the girl who nearly got into the trenches, dressed in her regulation uniform shortly after her arrival in New York.

Mrs. Carter cut her hair, donned an army uniform and boarded the train on which her husband and his regiment left Douglas, Arizona, for a port to embark for Europe. Not until she neared Chicago did her husband know of her acts and he then urged her to return home. Her identity was discovered by an officer on shipboard who happened to overhear HMIMMAGI her talking. Mrs. Carter's husband was a corporeal in his regiment. She says his stripes were taken from him on shipboard. Mrs. Carter is small, vivacious, and twenty-two years of age.
This photograph was made today, July 17th, shortly after her arrival in New York and shows her as she appeared in soldier dress.
